fields.affectedArea: All customers in the Eastside pressure zone (east of the Mill River, including Cedar Heights and the Harbor Industrial Park)
fields.whatHappened: Water samples collected on October 20 from two sites in the Eastside pressure zone tested positive for E. coli bacteria. The Eastside booster station also lost pressure for about six hours on October 19 after a control-system failure. These bacteria can make you sick, and are a particular concern for people with weakened immune systems.
whatToDo: DO NOT DRINK THE WATER WITHOUT BOILING IT FIRST. Bring all water to a boil, let it boil for one minute, and let it cool before using, or use bottled water.
Use boiled or bottled water for drinking, making ice, brushing teeth, washing dishes and food preparation until further notice.
Boiling kills bacteria and other organisms in the water.
Bottled water is available at Riverbend Community Center, 1200 Lake Ave, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
fields.whatIsBeingDone: We are flushing water mains, increasing chlorine levels and collecting additional samples throughout the Eastside zone. The booster station is running in manual control while the cause of the failure is investigated.
fields.expectedResolution: We will tell you when you no longer need to boil your water. We anticipate resolving the problem within 3 days.
